title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Faster editing, visual structure, cleaner projects
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.34.0 adds a fast editing toolkit, new structure views, static execution checks, and dead weight detection, plus a semantic highlighting fix.

highlights.title: Fast Editing Toolkit
highlights.description: Named arguments, postfix completion, live templates, surround with, and smart join lines bring familiar IntelliJ editing gestures straight to the lightbulb.

highlights.title: New Structure Views
highlights.description: Compose Outline, Android project view, Screen Flow Map, and UDF X-Ray sit in a dedicated view container, mapping app structure without a build.

highlights.title: Static Execution Checks
highlights.description: Lifecycle pairing, dispatcher lens, and Room migration drift catch lifecycle leaks, dispatcher misuse, and schema drift before the code ever runs.

sections.heading: Improvements
bullets: Added a fast editing toolkit (named arguments, postfix completion, live templates, surround with, smart join lines) that brings common IntelliJ gestures to the lightbulb, cutting down repetitive edits.
Added a dedicated view container with Compose Outline, Android project view, Screen Flow Map, and UDF X-Ray, showing app structure without running a build.
Added static execution checks for lifecycle pairing, dispatcher misuse, and Room migration drift, surfacing bugs that would otherwise only appear at runtime.
Added dead weight detection with usage badges on resources, dependencies, and manifest entries, each with a quick fix to remove what is unused.
Added resource tools (extract string resource, resource shadowing, reverse string map, hardcoded string lint) and a quick fix sweep for expired TODOs, unsafe !! assertions, and missing when branches.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fixed semantic highlighting so declaration tokens stay accurate after unsaved edits and multiline strings mask correctly, keeping colors reliable while typing.
